newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia will have to reform taxation system - PM.
newsitem.headline: Australia will have to reform taxation system - PM.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, in his strongest comments yet on tax reform, has said the Australian taxation system would have to be reformed at some stage.

"I wouldn't yet start getting time specific about that, but there's no doubt that at some stage, sooner or later, we will have to reform the Australian taxation system," Howard said on the Seven Network's Face to Face programme on Sunday.
He had been asked when the government would look at introducing a Goods and Services Tax (GST).
The conservative Liberal/National government promised before the March 1996 election not to introduce a GST, but has since qualified that promise by saying it applied to its first term of government.
The government is widely seen softening the ground for taxation reform and some type of GST to be introduced if it wins the election scheduled for the first half of 1999.

In late January Howard said Australia had a less than perfect taxation system and that he had not lost interest in reform. But he also said then a GST was decisively rejected at the 1993 election and it was not clear that voters had changed
Polls have recently shown support for a GST rising and several community groups have reversed their opposition to a GST.
Howard said on Sunday he had been a consistent supporter of tax reform, although he was concious of his committment not to introduce such reform in the current term of parliament.
"But if you're saying to me, do I envisage the Australian taxation system remaining as it is for the next five or ten years, I'd have to say no."
